mathematical_review.scope: Mathematical source and proof review for the selected branches, not a review of complete research proofs.

parent.otto: Read all 25 atoms, overview and reference. Checked metric gradients, continuity and constrained dissipation, finite-mass transport scaling, rarefaction signs and front speeds, low-regularity product counterexample, Gaussian semigroup proof, formal multi-index finiteness, polynomial recentering and reconstruction uniqueness. Independently checked LOTT §§2.2.5–2.3, including the transpose convention and uniform moment constants. JKO and LOTT research existence results remain citations.
parent.buffa: Read all 18 atoms, overview and reference. Checked inverse-map cofactor formula, Cordes perturbation constants, curvature identity, residual recovery using surjectivity, conforming Galerkin and residual bounds, interface Hessian sign and determinant homotopy. General convex-domain regularity and RKC remain cited inputs.
parent.ziegler: Read 2900–2903, 4Z01–4Z0D and reference. Checked the three Cauchy–Schwarz steps, cyclic cube lifting, inverse-theorem quantifier order, ordinary/logarithmic summation by parts and word-indicator expansion. Independently checked MRTTZ v3 Corollaries 1.6 and 1.11 and Theorem 1.9 against the exact claims. No full GTZ/MRTTZ research-proof review.

independent_reviews.result: No mathematical correction or citation-boundary issue found within the reviewed range.
independent_reviews.limits: No complete DG convergence-theory review, build or browser validation.

findings.issue: G acts on coefficient families; it is the algebraic transpose of the degree-lowering operator on T. A degree-one input coefficient contributes 2 to degree two for displacement (1,0).
findings.correction: Parent replaced the operator statement with the precise row/column condition, defined the underlying operator and its dual action, and supplied the degree-one/degree-two example.

findings.original_claim: The polynomial model gives a finite-dimensional prototype.
findings.issue: The untruncated polynomial sector is infinite-dimensional.
findings.correction: Parent restricted finite dimensionality to finite-degree truncations and explicitly identified the infinite untruncated sector.

independent_reviews.other_results: No other substantive error found: counterterm sign/support, coefficientwise finite sums, cocycle and moment-constant dependence agree with the original statement. Smooth linearisation and reconstruction uniqueness are valid.
independent_reviews.limits: No review of LOTT §§3–8 deep proofs, video timestamps or rendered pages.

followup.result: Both findings are resolved. The transpose index convention agrees with LOTT footnote 41. The explanatory link from 4X0J to 4X0N is not registered as a prerequisite and introduces no prerequisite cycle.
followup.additional_clarification: 4X0N now spells out the source convention: G_xy=(Gamma_yx)*, denoted Gamma_xy* by LOTT with swapped indices in footnote 41.
followup.regression: tests/plenary-otto-math.test.mjs explicitly distinguishes basis-vector and dual coefficient directions.

mathematical_review.report_reading_boundary: Otto automatic captions were read, with precise mathematics sourced separately. Buffa and Ziegler official videos were sampled at documented slide points; neither is registered as a complete lecture reading.
